requirement_or_question: ExtractionPolicy symlinks: Refuse, Safe (default) or All. Safe accepts only relative targets whose lexical resolution from the link's parent stays beneath the root, refusing '/'-rooted and (on Windows) backslash or drive targets without rewriting; All is the explicit opt-in for exact absolute or escaping targets. SPEC instead writes absolute targets as-is with no policy; incumbents refuse (Python data filter) or resolve in-root (openat2 recommendation).

Pre-existing destination links and concurrent attackers are not covered by the argument.

SPEC fixes only ACL-last ordering; a complete per-platform order (capabilities, immutable flags, SELinux labels, Windows attributes and SDs, ACL inheritance) is unspecified.

Selective extraction's handling of excluded ancestors is unspecified.

requirement_or_question: Archive validity and extraction safety are separate: a valid archive may be refused or partially restored by extraction policy. SPEC's formal losslessness contract covers only File and Symlink and says there is no mode in which it fails, leaving open whether refused or renamed extraction is a contract violation, a declared fidelity gap, or out of scope.

Each MetadataItem carries namespace, name, typed value, criticality (Critical or Optional), restore class (Restorable, CaptureOnly, PlatformSpecific) and fidelity declaration; each registered name carries type, default criticality, restorability and identity participation. The implementation fixes restorability per name (macos.birthtime CaptureOnly) and MetadataItem v1-v3 select value fields from a closed registry; a per-timestamp restorable bool overlaps the restore class.

requirement_or_question: POSIX1E ACLs are ALLOW-only rwx entries in canonical principal order with exactly one USER_OBJ, GROUP_OBJ and OTHER and MASK iff named entries exist; NFS4 permissions use mask 0x001f01ff; principals are numeric ids or UUIDs only. Windows descriptors are exact validated self-relative bytes (SID revision 1, at most 15 subauthorities, ACL revision 2 or 4, ACE types 0x00-0x15) with ACE and DACL/SACL order preserved and no POSIX translation; unknown ACE types are NONCONFORMING.
